preamble.text: Reach the lighthouse before the tide turns

items.text: Dawn. Fog sits on the water. MARGOT, the harbour keeper, is mending a net and does not look up. Plays when the player first arrives.

items.speaker: MARGOT
items.text: You've come down the salt road. Nobody does that any more.
I need to reach the lighthouse.

items.speaker: MARGOT
items.text: Then you need the key, and the key is with Tam.
Why is the harbour empty?

items.speaker: MARGOT
items.text: The boats went out after the light went dark. None came back.
Never mind.

items.speaker: MARGOT
items.text: Mind the wet planks.

items.speaker: MARGOT
items.text: Fog is thicker than it was.
The salt road runs along the bar at low water. It is dry for four hours a day, and not one minute more.
A loft of drying nets. TAM, young and out of breath, hides a brass key behind his back.

items.speaker: TAM
items.text: Margot sent you? She always sends someone. They never come back.
The boats never came back either. I know.

items.speaker: TAM
items.text: Then you know why I am scared of that light.
Give me the key.

items.speaker: TAM
items.text: Take it. Please. Just take it.
I will leave you to it.

items.speaker: TAM
items.text: Is somebody there?
The tide is already lapping at the steps. The door is stiff, and the lamp room above is dark.

items.speaker: TAM
items.text: I will hold the door. Go on.
Climb to the lamp room.
Turn back.
